title: Authorize module-backed Skills using concrete Module capabilities
goal: Ensure M6 authorization for a module-backed Skill includes the actual capability declared by its bound Module contract.
context: M6 proposals for module-backed Skills currently use manifest capabilities. The built-in workspace.create-file manifest can declare read/execute while its bound Module requires write, so M6 authorization does not reflect the full effective capability set.
forbidden_changes: Do not infer module bindings from arbitrary metadata; use the existing exact built-in Skill-to-Module binding.
Do not weaken ModuleRuntime policy or approval checks.
Do not modify UI, provider/GGUF, or workspace path validation.
acceptance_criteria: Exact built-in module-backed Skills derive effective capabilities from manifest requirements union the matching Module contract capabilities union execute.
Schema or binding mismatch fails closed.
M6 rejects an authorization set that differs from effective Skill capabilities.
Regression proves workspace.create-file authorization includes read, write, and execute rather than the stale manifest read/execute set.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If a built-in Skill cannot resolve its exact Module contract, keep it unavailable and repair the binding/schema fixture rather than falling back to manifest-declared capabilities.
